plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets capital preservation with a potential ~1.5%/month return. It significantly de-risks the portfolio by cutting all leveraged ETFs and reducing concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 1% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Buy SLB at 4% and XLV at 5% to add strong scanner long setups.
Sell QQQ and SMH to exit flagged downtrend and below stop positions.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for risk-first growth, targeting ~2.5%/month. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing new, high-scoring long setups. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, balancing growth with risk management.

plan: Add to SOXL and SPAL, targeting 6% each, to increase leveraged ETF exposure.
Buy SLB at 8% and COIN at 5% to concentrate in high-scoring long setups.
Trim SMH to 5% to reduce exposure to a below-stop position.
Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single name mandate.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets stretch growth, aiming for ~4%/month. It leans into leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring scanner setups. Be aware this strategy significantly raises both upside potential and drawdown risk, with leveraged ETFs subject to daily decay and rebalancing. Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage potential rapid losses.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETFs.
Add to QQQI, targeting 30%, to rotate into income-focused ETFs.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Sell QQQ and CRWD to exit broad index and high-beta single names.
Sell SMH to exit the flagged below stop position.
income.read: This income plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions, targeting ~1%/month. It rotates heavily into income ETFs and cuts leverage and high-beta names. While aiming for low drawdown and reliable income, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
